branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Subcutaneous Axillary Tumor with Epithelial Features

state.case_summary:
A woman in her 60s presented with a slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla that she first noticed 10 years ago, with progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year. She reported experiencing swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago that disappeared with lactation, followed by mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles.

Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm

static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla for 10 years
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Punch Biopsy: dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Immunohistochemistry: Negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Excision Findings: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
Lymph Node Analysis: 1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Imaging Studies: Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors
Figure A: Clinical photograph shows erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring about 5 × 3 cm
Figure B: Histopathology from skin punch biopsy showing dense dermal infiltrates of atypical epithelioid tumor cells with basophilic nuclei dispersed between collagen fibers in an Indian file pattern
Figure C: Histopathology from complete tumor excision showing closely associated apocrine glands apart from diffuse infiltrates of tumor cells
Figure D: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating GATA3-positive apocrine glandular structures
